changes.summary: Known as one of the most influential artists of our time, Jenny Holzer places words and ideas at the heart of her thought-provoking practice. For the museum wide activation "J'ai vu", conceived for and with the Musée d’Orsay for fall 2026, Holzer offers text fragments from the Musée d’Orsay’s archive and the historical period covered by its collection, disseminated across her signature media: monumental installations, projections onto the historic façade of the former railway station, engravings on exotic stone, and luminous electronic displays. The exhibition at the Musée d’Orsay will adopt diverse forms, beginning with light projections on the museum’s façade along the Seine timed to coincide with the show’s opening in October. Excerpts selected by Holzer from a range of sources, from artist letters found in the museum’s archive to contemporaneous literary and political commentary, will transform the building’s exterior and offer time travel for passersby. Inside the museum, a site-specific LED animated with colorful streams of text will allow visitors to immerse themselves in content drawn from, and responding to, the history represented in the Musée d’Orsay’s collection. The LED echoes the building’s conversion from 19th - century railway station to modern museum: custom programming traversing the space mirrors the bustling visitor circulation and nods to the Gare d’Orsay’s original function. Streaming through an artist-curated presentation of collection works in the domed galleries of History Painting, Naturalism, and Symbolism, the LED will speak with Holzer’s gold, platinum, and palladium-leafed paintings. These metallic redaction paintings bring secrecy to the surface, and will change with the Seine’s light over the course of days. Much of the paintings’ content has been obscured, but vestiges of hard and necessary decisions remain, echoing the history paintings on view in adjacent galleries.
